# Scans {.unnumbered}

```{r set}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
```

## Raw

We first use the following bash code to aggregate images and convert pdf to png.

```         
cd data/derived/Belterra_2025/
mkdir pdfs
ls ../raw/Belterra_2025/scans/*/*
cp ../raw/Belterra_2025/scans/*/* pdfs
mkdirs pngs
for file in $(ls pdfs/)
do
  pdftoppm pdfs/$file pngs/$file -png
done
```

We then use ImageJ (<https://imagej.net/ij/download.html>) with the following steps:

- Open virtual stack
- Type \> 8-Bit
- Adjust \> Threshold \> Automatic
- Analyze Particles
  - Size: 1000-Infinity
  - Circularity: 0-1
  - Display results, clear results, exclude on edges, summarize, composite ROIs
  - with or without include holes depending on the question

The intermediate threshold images with detected are saved for manual check.

```{r data}
#| eval: false
la_ex <- read_csv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/area_excluded_summary.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_excluded = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_excluded = area_excluded / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_in <- read_csv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/area_included_summary.csv") %>% 
  select(Slice, `Total Area`) %>% 
  rename(slice = Slice, area_included = `Total Area`) %>% 
  separate(slice, c("vernacular", "tree", "leaf")) %>% 
  mutate(area_included = area_included / (1275*1755) * (21*29.7))
la_ex %>% 
  left_join(la_in) %>% 
  write_tsv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/la.tsv")
```

```{r figure}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
read_tsv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/la.tsv") %>% 
  group_by(vernacular) %>% 
  mutate(la_s = mean(area_included)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(vernacular = fct_reorder(vernacular, la_s)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(vernacular,
             area_included)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(col = as.factor(tree)),
              width = 0.2, size = 3) + 
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Vernacular name", y = "LA [ cm2 ]") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none") +
  scale_y_log10()
```

```{r problems}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
read_tsv("data/derived/Belterra_2025/la.tsv") %>% 
  filter(area_included < 1) %>% 
  knitr::kable()
```

> We have issues with ANGEL 5677 leaves 2 and 4 because scans are touching the border. I have no better solution than manually adding a black line in a photo editor to treat them beforehand.

## Manual check

```{r}
#| message: false
check <- read_csv("data/corrections/Belterra_2025/manual_check.csv")
```

Masks generated with the option allowing holes to be filled were manually inspected for (*NA* when no existing mask):

### Missing parts

- *missing_part*: missing part in the leave due to herbivory or other damage: *0* no missing part, *1* moderate missing part, and *2* big missing part (see [page junction](#incomplete_belt_2025) for the filtering out of leaves with a big missing part).

Number of leaves concerned by missing parts (per class):

```{r}
check %>% 
  count(vernacular, missing_part) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = missing_part,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

### Anomalies

- *anomaly*: any anomaly in the generated masks:

  - *ok*: no problem

  - *abn_area*: abnormal area are masked, detected because they don't have the shape of a leaf. Looking at the corresponding scan, it is because these areas correspond to some spaces between the folioles that are fully surrounded by leaf part. So they are interpreted as holes and filled.

  - *fol_touch*: this is the same problem than *abn_area*, except for the FAVA for which the foliolules are actually touching and form a compact area on the mask.

  - *miss_petiolul*: for double-compound leaves, the petiolule is not included, when it should have been

  - *petiol_included*: the petiole has been included, when it should not have

  - *one_fol*: just one foliole when the species has compound leaves

Number of leaves concerned by anomaly:

```{r}
check %>% 
  count(vernacular, anomaly) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = anomaly,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

> abn_area and fol_touch are actually the same problem (to do for the next campaign: change the manual check classification. To solve this problem, drawing a small line on the scan to avoid the petiole merging is possible for PARAP and COPAI (but that is not the one for which it matters the more), but not for FAVAO, FAVA and ANGEL. The decission is made to use the unfilled area even for LA. this will be implemented in the [page junction](#anomalie_belt_2025)

> Our protocol states that the petiole should be removed, and the petiolule should be included. In the cases when this is not respected (*petiol_included* or *miss_petiolul*),a nd in the base when just one foliole has been considered, we will remove the values of LA, LDMC and SLA, but LT and tlp. This will be done in the [page junction](#anomalie_belt_2025).

### Leaf touching the side of the scan

- *touching*: *0* no part touching, *1* leaf touching leading to part of the leaf not taken into account, *2* leaf touching leading to all the leaf not taken into account **=\> TO DO (Sylvain?) to be corrected by adding a black line with a photo editor?**

Number of leaves touching leaves:

```{r}
check %>% 
  count(vernacular, touching) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = touching,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

Here are the touching leaves:

```{r}
check %>% filter(touching %in% c(1,2))
```

Here is an example for each species and category:

### Damaged and young leaves

Raw leaf scans are manually checked for the following problems, but this is highly subjective:

- *ok*: no problem (or very small area concerned)

- *damaged*: part of the leaf or the whole leaf appears black/brown or yellowish on the scan or there are any other damages (except missing part of the leaf) suggesting that the leaf is decaying or is attacked by insects

- *young*: the bright green colour of the leave compared to the other leaves from the individual and/or the species suggest non mature leaves

Number of damaged or young leaves:

```{r}
check %>% 
  count(vernacular, raw_scan) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = raw_scan,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

## Corrections {#scan_cor_belt_2025}

Here is an automatic bash command to copy problematic files:

```{r}
command <- check %>% filter(touching %in% c(1,2)) |> 
  mutate(file = paste0(vernacular, "_", tree, "_", leaf, ".pdf-1.png")) |> 
  mutate(file = paste0("data/derived/Belterra_2025/pngs/", file)) |> 
  summarise(command = paste0("cp ",
                             paste(file, collapse = " "),
                             " data/corrections/Belterra_2025/pngs"))
cat(command$command)
```

We then use ImageJ (<https://imagej.net/ij/download.html>) with the following steps:

- Open virtual stack
- Type \> 8-Bit
- Adjust \> Threshold \> Automatic
- Analyze Particles
  - Size: 1000-Infinity
  - Circularity: 0-1
  - Show: Overlay Masks
  - Display results, clear results, **do not exclude on edges**, summarize, composite ROIs
  - with or without include holes depending on the question
- Export Image sequence to save the masks

The intermediate threshold images with detected are saved for manual check.

`CASTA_6568_2.pdf-1.png` still had an issue because extra objects appeared on the edge due to shadows and needed to be manually modified.
